prerequisites: Lecture "Introduction to Artificial Intelligence" from the 1st semester of the Bachelor's degree program "Artificial Intelligence" (especially basics in the R programming language, basic knowledge of data analysis and machine learning)

learning_outcomes.text: Students understand the broad spectrum of techniques, methods and applications of Machine Learning.
Students have the ability to create AI systems using Machine Learning with suitable software.
Students have the ability to evaluate the applicability of Machine Learning for specific problems in companies and select appropriate methods.
Students can implement their own methods and defend them against competing approaches.
Students can present results created in group work and discuss developed solutions with other students.

syllabus_topics: Statistical Key Figures and Exploratory Data Analysis
Evaluation of Forecasts: Quality Measures in Supervised Learning
Universal Consistency and Model Selection (e.g.: Additive Models with L2-Boosting)
Unsupervised Learning: Cluster Analysis with the k-Means Algorithm
teaching_methods: Practical tasks on real datasets at the computer
bibliography: Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jerome Friedman (2009): The Elements of Statistical Learning. Springer, New York
Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani (2017): An Introduction to Statistical Learning: with Applications in R. Springer, New York
